text:
kai: seeing a spike in internal DNS timeouts across east-west traffic between gpu pools -> core services. App-level retries are amplifying load, lots of 5xx from peer calls. noticed from kube-proxy logs and app traces :eyes:
chen: any pattern on pod/node boundary? same AZ or cross-AZ?
sara: appears mostly same-AZ but also some cross-node within same rack. p95 latency to node-local-dns jumped from 5ms -> 200-400ms for short bursts.
alex: logs show a bunch of UDP truncation and retries, possible fragmentation/mtu issue. also seeing RDMA NICs fall back to UDP in some hosts (driver logs).
kai: here's a short tcpdump snippet from a problematic node (redacted):
```
17:42:01.123456 IP 10.233.45.12.5353 > 10.233.1.5.49732: UDP, length 1452
17:42:01.124789 IP 10.233.45.12.5353 > 10.233.1.5.49732: UDP, length 1452 (retrans)
17:42:01.130001 IP 10.233.1.5.49732 > 10.233.45.12.5353: ICMP frag needed mtu=9000
```
mike: icmp frag needed -> MTU mismatch. Are we doing MTU clamping on some hosts (vf, hostdev, veth)?
chen: we recently rolled kernel driver update on some RDMA hosts two nights ago. suspecting a regression that clobbers path MTU for east-west SR-IOV paths.
sara: node-local-dns cache also seems to be evicting aggressively — cache misses spike when egress retries happen. that increases query fanout to CoreDNS and we're hitting CoreDNS tail.
alex: short-term mitigation: lower dns cache TTL at node-local-dns? or increase cache size to avoid upstream storm. Also rate-limit client-side retries (we have a global setting in sidecars).
kai: can we flip a gateway-level MTU clamp to 9000->1500 on the affected rack to see if it stops fragmentation?
mike: yes we can, but would need a rolling change on the switch and host configs. risk for other workloads. suggest doing canary on 2 nodes first.
infra-bot: incident create: INT-2026-1987 created, assigned to eng-infra oncall. See runbook: /runbooks/dns-frag-eastwest
chen: tests to run: iperf mtu test between two gpu nodes, `tracepath` to see pmtu hops, `ethtool -k` to check offloads, and kernel dmesg for rdma driver EFAULT.
sara: temporary routing: route internal service calls through an ALB in another AZ (adds latency but reduces retries) — we can flip that for high QPS routes.
alex: also adding a CoreDNS horizontal pod autoscaler for p99 load bursts might help. not a fix for the root cause but buys time.
kai: action items: 1) chen -> roll canary MTU clamp on 2 nodes (in next 15m) 2) mike -> run iperf + tracepath across sample nodes 3) sara -> bump node-local-dns cache size and enable short-term TTL 4) alex -> add temporary HPA for coredns 5) mike/chen -> capture RDMA driver logs and vendor bug report if reproduces
chen: starting canary now, will post results.
mike: running iperf, sharing results in 5m :white_check_mark:
chen: canary MTU clamp applied to node-22 and node-23, monitoring.
sara: cache size bumped + TTL=30s applied to node-local-dns on canary nodes.
kai: if mitigation holds for 10m we can roll further, otherwise rollback. thanks all :thumbsup:
alex: if anyone sees retries still amplifying, add small jitter to client retry backoff to smooth the spike.
infra-bot: incident updated: mitigation deployed to canary nodes, monitoring 10m.
